From a post-merge code review of the batter-oj37 change (merged as d0064cdc), relevant to this issue; passed on as reported, not re-verified by me beyond reading the code path: (1) through TestClient::request a reused map also reaches operational_http_with_quota, which calls replace_quota on the inherited shared ObservationState, so the SOURCE request's completion event can report the destination's quota facts, in addition to the appended captures, concatenated MatchedPath and missing completion event already described here. fields.description: batter_axum::low_level::RouterClient::request (shared by InProcessClient and batter_runlimit::http::TestClient) detects only Axum routing records (RawPathParams record, MatchedPath, NestedPath, OriginalUri). A map that carries Batter's own ObservationState/OperationalScope (and CorrelationId) with no detected Axum record is accepted, and the observer and correlation layers keep the inherited records and install none. Reproduced by hand through TestClient on Axum 0.8.9 (gp93 branch, PR #117): a map captured in a protected custom root fallback for OPTIONS * carries OriginalUri as its only detected record; with OriginalUri removed by the caller the request is authenticated (1->2) and charged one native quota check (1->2), answers 200 with no x-request-id, the handler sees the client's unreplaced inbound x-request-id, and no completion event is emitted. The same residual applies to InProcessClient without the quota cost (batter-oj37 recorded it as out of scope). Batter's private record types live in batter-axum, so RouterClient could detect them at entry. Documented today on RouterClient::request, TestClient::request, guarantees (native quota execution, HTTP boundary) and integrations.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Decide whether the entry check also refuses requests carrying Batter's private observation/operational/correlation records (or another library-owned handling) without deleting application metadata; enforce it in RouterClient so both clients inherit it; cover the OPTIONS * fallback map with OriginalUri removed through InProcessClient and TestClient, including no quota consumed; update the residual statements in rustdoc, guarantees, integrations, READMEs and CHANGELOG; run scripts/verify.sh.
fields.title: Refuse or reset inherited Batter records in in-process requests

fields.description: batter_runlimit::http::HttpQuota::prepare orders batter_axum::low_level middleware itself (request_admission -> authentication -> native atomic quota -> body), because HttpBoundary cannot place an authenticated quota stage between admission and body extraction. As a result its TestClient holds a low-level RouterClient (gp93) rather than the sealed InProcessClient, and serving uses low_level::register_http_with_connect_info_in. Code review of gp93 raised the altitude point: a library-owned quota stage in HttpBoundary (or a route-group policy hook) would let Runlimit's assembly be a sealed boundary and drop its caller-ordered low_level composition. Evaluate under ADR-010; proposed, not designed.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Produce an ADR-010 assessment of whether HttpBoundary (or RouteGroup policy) can own an authenticated pre-body quota stage without weakening existing sealed-assembly invariants; if adopted, migrate HttpQuota to it with failure-path tests, CHANGELOG hard-cut notes as required, and verification; if rejected, record the evidence-backed reason.
fields.title: Express Runlimit's quota stage inside HttpBoundary so its client is a real InProcessClient

fields.description: A post-merge xhigh code review of the batter-oj37 change (master d0064cdc) found gaps to close in one follow-up PR. (1) The entry check looks only for Axum routing records, although batter-axum can name its own private request records. Reviewer-confirmed with a throwaway test: a map captured in the fallback of an OPTIONS * dispatch with the public OriginalUri removed is accepted; the destination answers 200 with the earlier request's correlation id, no x-request-id and no completion event. Decision: refuse such a request whole at entry as well (refusing, not clearing, stays within the batter-oj37 contract). (2) A live request forwarded by an outer Axum router into the client (Router fallback, route or nest_service closure) is now refused on every request; reviewer-confirmed. Decision: keep refusing, because that shape carries outer routing state and serves the boundary outside protected registration, but docs/guarantees.md still says the contract does not constrain 'an application's own transport wrapper' and the migration text covers only the stale-clone shape; state the rule and the migration. (3) CHANGELOG, guarantees and integrations claim the reference service's request client inherits the refusal with no executable test or unverified label. (4) The detection claim rests on Axum 0.8.9 internals while the crate's requirement allows later 0.8.x; record that it is verified for 0.8.9 only. (5) Documentation: the struct doc still says synthetic extensions are the caller's choice although a hand-inserted OriginalUri is refused; the refusal cannot be identified by status or body, only by the marker. (6) Test tidy: completions() is defined three times in tests/route_groups. COORDINATION: PR 117 (batter-gp93, another session) moves the entry check into low_level::RouterClient and rewrites the same rustdoc, docs and CHANGELOG passages, and documents item (1) as an uncovered residual; this work must be based on or rebased over it.
fields.acceptance_criteria: A request carrying any Batter-private request record with no detected Axum record is refused whole at entry with the same marker, before the router or application code is polled, with a failure-path test for the OPTIONS * map with OriginalUri removed and for a map captured behind a low_level wrapper; accepted requests and application extensions are unaffected. The forwarded-live-request refusal is pinned by a test and stated in rustdoc, contract documents and CHANGELOG with its migration. The reference service's client has a reused-map test and its rustdoc states the precondition. The Axum-version limit is recorded. Contract documents, status row, assessment and CHANGELOG agree with the code. Required verification runs and its outcome is recorded here.

fields.title: Settle owned-body framing by transport containment; fix third xhigh review findings

data.text:
ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment (2026-11-15), triggered by the third xhigh /code-review of the branch (10 findings) after review-fix rounds 35e5cf90, 481da188, 29326d94, b6efd60a and 7d613f02 each repaired owned-body framing settlement.

1. Recurring defects. Confirmed in source and Hyper 1.11.1 dispatch.rs:356-447: (a) source_end asks is_end_stream before the recorded refusal, so an already-ended body under a refused head (final 1xx but 101, CONNECT 2xx with a length header) is completed, not failed; (b) Framing freezes on the first poll by anyone, so a handler or inner layer that polls once ignores later Content-Length, admission's settle and the server's refusal; (c) admission polled on another task (tokio::spawn(next.run)) never sees the server's task-local and is pinned by a test to a wrong completed; (d) BodyStart::unserved hides the server's record from an in-process dispatch inside a served handler, so a proxied in-process response is framed by the default inner head. (d) is the mirror image of the previous round's fix (an in-process body kept by the handler was settled by the outer head). Unconfirmed until executed: none of (a)-(d) was run before this assessment; the review supplied scenarios.
2. Invariant trace. The completion event's completed/failed/dropped must follow the head Hyper writes for the message that carries the body. The public API enforces none of the association; it is inferred privately from which response future's task-local was current when admission ran (execution context), not from which written response contains the body (containment). Owner: batter-axum (adapter design); the encode rules are upstream (Hyper, private).
3. Classification. Library/adapter design gap: each local repair re-chose which of two compositions the execution-context association gets wrong (kept vs proxied in-process bodies; same-task vs spawned admission). Another patch (extension fallback for (c), relinking for (d)) covers another case of the same protocol and flips the opposite case. Upstream complexity also present: Hyper exposes no encode decision, so the length/refusal mirror of role.rs stays; real-socket tests remain its guard.
4. Remedy (bounded, no public signature change, removes two documented low-level caller obligations): associate by containment. completion::Responding computes the written framing (length, refusal) from the request head and the response it hands Hyper; ConnectionBody scopes a thread-local around every call Hyper makes into the response body (poll_frame, is_end_stream, size_hint, destruction); an OwnedBody reached inside that scope adopts the written framing once and keeps it. Admission's own framing remains the fallback off the registered server. Removes the SERVING task-local, linked records, BodyStart::unserved and the any-poller freeze. Residual limits to disclose: a body polled from another task by a body layer (channel pump) is not reached through the transport and keeps admission's framing; bytes are counted at the owned body, so a layer that adds or transforms bytes under a declared length, or a message joining several bodies, is judged against the whole message (pre-existing). Independent fixes in the same round: (a) ordering, stop_clock doctest flake and rustdoc, stale Start::claimed doc, settle_with double lock.

Implemented (working tree on 29326d94, uncommitted). batter-axum: streaming/start.rs replaces the SERVING task-local, linked records, claim/served/unserved and settle_written with Written (framing + refusal from the request head and the response handed to Hyper) and a thread-local scope; serving/completion.rs Responding computes Written, ConnectionBody scopes it around poll_frame, is_end_stream, size_hint and destruction (inner Option dropped inside the scope, token released after); OwnedBody adopts it in each call and in Drop, once; the any-poller freeze and OwnedBody.polled are removed; source_end checks the recorded refusal first; BodyStart keeps continuation and a OnceLock framing (settle asks size_hint before any lock, no Vec clone, F9); boundary/client.rs back to plain oneshot. batter-core: forced_cancellation_at rustdoc states it is recorded when the drain phase ends (allowance or earlier once every direct task finished, driver delay can make it later); doctest asserts forced + allowance >= abort (cannot flake); tests/lifecycle.rs forced_cancellation_begins_when_the_drain_phase_ends pins both paths on a paused clock. Tests: start_tests rewritten (adoption once, scope restore incl. unwind, refusal only from Written, request-head framing); sockets/framing: 103 refusal for pending, ended (F1) and handler-polled (F2) bodies, spawned admission now failed (F3), returned in-process response failed (F4); destruction: in-process poll-before-transport leaves the declared length to admission (F2). Mutation checks by hand, reverted: disabling adoption failed 7 framing socket cases incl. spawned and returned in-process; end-before-refusal failed the ended 103 case; freeze-on-any-poll failed the in-process poll-before-transport and handler-polled 103 cases. Docs: README, CHANGELOG, guarantees.md, references/http.md, crate AGENTS.md, register_http/request_admission/low_level/into_streaming_response rustdoc; disclosed residual limits: a body a layer polls on another task than the connection's keeps admission's framing; bytes are counted at the owned body. Verification: bash scripts/verify.sh (Rust 1.98.1) exit 0: 4835 passed, 0 failed, 438 ignored, all HTTP smoke profiles PASS; check_file_budget no errors. A CHANGELOG-only wording fix (per-request overhead) followed the run. Not committed or pushed. Hosted CI, macOS, HTTP/2 not claimed.

fields.title: Final Codex review of 9wig branch: nested in-process framing leak and ended-body refusal mirror

data.text:
Final pre-merge review (2026-11-16): codex review, gpt-6-astra, xhigh, range d0064cdc..9023b1e1. Verdict: not merge-ready. Codex ran focused axum/core tests and doctests (pass) and reports real-socket reproductions; Claude confirmed both findings by source reading, not by rerunning the reproductions.
(A) P2 start.rs:143-149: Written is current for the whole synchronous transport call, so application code nested in it (an owned or unowned stream that calls InProcessClient::request during poll_frame) lets an unrelated inner owned body adopt the outer message's framing via admission's size query. Regression introduced by 9023b1e1 (the task-local design scoped only response production, not body polls). ADR-010 trigger: a repair introduced a confirmed failure in the coupled framing phase.
(B) P2 start.rs:109-113: Hyper 1.11.1 role.rs:698-830 writes an is_end_stream body with msg.body == None, skipping Content-Length (not parsed, wrote_len unset unless HEAD) before any conflict check and dropping Transfer-Encoding in HTTP/1.0; Head::refused ignores that branch, so an ended body under CL-before-TE (HTTP/1.0), an unparsable or conflicting CL is reported failed though Hyper sends a complete response. Pre-existing mirror gap (upstream protocol complexity).
(C) P3 docs/references/http.md:624 trailing blank line from af5f5f7a.
Assessment: (A) cause is the scope of the containment marker ('inside a transport call') rather than 'in the transport's body chain'. Bounded remedy: OwnedBody clears the marker while running application code (source poll, queries, destruction) so only the outermost owned body in the chain adopts, and in-process dispatch (InProcessClient, RouterClient after merging origin/master) polls its dispatch with the marker cleared. Residual to disclose: an in-process body consumed by unowned application body code or a body layer inside a transport call still adopts; call-stack containment cannot tell consuming code from forwarding layers. Alternative (larger, not recommended now): judge message completeness at ConnectionBody from bytes Hyper received and report it only to the first owned body. (B) remedy: take Hyper's is_end_stream answer in Written::of and model the None-body branch (CL ignored except under HEAD; TE-before-CL in a chunkable answer still refuses). Awaiting user decision before dependent repairs; origin/master (6e4d926c, PR #117) also conflicts in CHANGELOG.md.

User approved the remedy (2026-11-16). Merged origin/master 6e4d926c locally as c33496a7 (CHANGELOG conflict only, both entries kept). Fix commit 1e19e1fd: (A) OwnedBody runs source polls, queries, destruction and discarded answers with no Written current (Written::outside via OwnedBody::application), so only the outermost owned body in the transport chain adopts; Framing::started records whether a framing was current at start and such a nested body never adopts; disclosed residual: a plain stream or body layer that consumes an owned body started elsewhere still lets it adopt. (B) Head::refused takes Option<&SizeHint> as Hyper passes msg.body; Written::of asks is_end_stream first; None branch: CL skipped unparsed, HEAD writes first CL and refuses a later length header, TE before CL in a chunkable answer refused. (C) trailing blank line removed. Tests: unit an_ended_body_is_refused_only_as_hyper_writes_it_as_none; sockets an_ended_body_under_a_head_refused_for_a_pending_one_is_completed, a_body_started_by_a_stream_hyper_polls_is_no_part_of_its_message, a_body_an_owned_source_forwards_keeps_its_own_framing. Mutation checks by hand, reverted: nested bodies adopting failed the polled-stream case; no clearing for owned sources failed the forwarded case; ignoring the end failed the ended HTTP/1.0 case. Verification: bash scripts/verify.sh (Rust 1.98.1) on 1e19e1fd's tree exit 0: 4858 passed, 0 failed, 438 ignored, 5 HTTP smoke profiles PASS; clippy and file budget clean. Confirming codex review (gpt-6-astra xhigh, 6e4d926c..HEAD) running. Not pushed.

Confirming review: codex review, gpt-6-astra, xhigh, range 6e4d926c..1e19e1fd: no actionable defects; Codex reports A and B match the pinned upstream sources and both regression tests fail with their fixes removed (its own run of axum tests, focused core tests and doctests in /tmp; it did not run the full matrix). Verdict: merge-ready. origin/master still 6e4d926c and contained in the branch. Branch is 8 commits ahead of origin/fix/http-forced-close-9wig; not pushed.

Design: judge owned-body outcomes by what the body observes, not a Hyper encoder mirror

data.text: Proposed, unexecuted. Source: second xhigh /code-review of the branch (2026-11-16), findings judged a recurring pattern under ADR-010 after batter-9wig.8 and .9. (1) streaming.rs OwnedBody::is_end_stream/size_hint adopt the current Written permanently: a plain stream that only queries an owned body started outside any transport call, while Hyper polls the stream, binds it to that message (the disclosed consuming-code residual). (2) start.rs Head::length/refused mirror Hyper 1.11.1's private encoder, but batter-axum declares no hyper dependency, so published consumers resolve any hyper 1.x and outcomes can drift silently (1.12.0 is published). (3) A declared Content-Length above the body's exact size: Hyper frames by the exact size and stops without asking for the end, so the body is reported dropped (INFO) rather than failed; Hyper debug builds assert on this mismatch. Alternative to assess: report only body-observable facts (the source ended, trailers, the transport asked for the end, or dropped after N bytes with the exact size or declared length produced) and drop the refusal/length mirror, or guard the mirror by the resolved hyper version. Changes documented completed/failed/dropped semantics; needs an ADR-010 assessment and user decision before implementation.

Proposed, unexecuted. Source: second xhigh /code-review (2026-11-16). (1) low_level.rs request_admission_inner allocates BodyStart (Arc, Mutex, OnceLock, Method clone) and an OperationContinuation before admitted::record, which discards both without server correlation; build them inside record only when the Admission is inserted. (2) completion.rs Written::of queries the application body's end and size and scans headers for every response, including ones with no owned body; measure, and consider a lazy computation. (3) batter-core lifecycle/state.rs abort_before nearly duplicates stop_before's notify loop; express it through stop_before or a shared wait helper. (4) lifecycle/capability.rs ShutdownSignal::observing duplicates LifecycleCoordinator::signal(); route both through one constructor.

(1) HTTP/2: start.rs answered() keeps a non-HTTP/1 request's own version and Head::http1() gates length and refusal, so only HTTP/1.0/1.1 requests (the versions Hyper's HTTP/1 server parses; role.rs:428-435 writes an HTTP/2-built response as HTTP/1.1) get the mirror; Axum 0.8.9 serve uses hyper-util's auto builder without http1_only (serve/mod.rs:391-394). Unit test only_an_http1_request_is_framed_by_hyper_http1_rules; HTTP/2 serving still unexercised. (2) Idle bound: an unarmed wait starts at the poll that begins it (overdue(asked), wait(cx, asked)), so a long synchronous poll straight after a frame ends at idle_timeout; bounds/answers outlasting-poll test now covers waits=false. (3) tests/operational/forced_close.rs zero-allowance abort test parametrized over register_http and register_http_with_connect_info_in (restores coverage removed in a5283127). fields.title: Fourth review: trailers end the owned body, empty-frame bound recheck, late-start dispatcher, shared head answers, carried-body settle, upgrade I/O recovery

data.text:
Six review findings (2026-11-18), all confirmed against source and repaired on fix/http-forced-close-9wig:
(1) streaming.rs: an owned body now ends when it yields trailers (yielded_end), so a holder that polls on gets None without the source being asked again; the trailers flag is gone.
(2) streaming.rs: after destroying a swallowed final empty frame and asking the source for its end, both bounds are checked again before the end is accepted.
(3) observation.rs: the request observer's dispatcher lives in the shared ObservationState apart from the span and beyond the observer, so a start refused after the response reports to the request's subscriber, without its span.
(4) start.rs/completion.rs: HeadAnswers is asked once in Responding; Written is computed from it and ConnectionBody gives Hyper the same end/size answers until the first poll.
(5) start.rs: BodyStart::settle settles only when admission's size query of the returned response reaches the started body (thread-local reach check by framing identity). Disclosed residual: off the registered server, a body behind a layer that answers the size query itself keeps its build-time framing.
(6) forced_close.rs: ForcedCloseIo is public as low_level::ForcedCloseIo with get_ref/into_inner (ADR-010 review: low-level escape hatch, obligations in rustdoc, no root alias, compile_fail control, no mutable access). Breaking: CHANGELOG entry with before/after; no deprecated shim possible (no Batter item removed). hyper/hyper-util added as dev-dependencies only, without http2.
BodyBudget moved to streaming/budget.rs to keep streaming.rs under the 800-line budget.
Tests: tests/streaming/endings.rs (4), tests/streaming/sockets/head.rs (1), tests/operational/forced_close/upgraded.rs (2), completion_tests.rs (2), start_tests.rs (1 new, 1 adapted). The four endings tests and the head socket test were run against the pre-fix source and failed there.

New evidence from batter-9wig.14 (2026-11-18), recorded under the ADR-010 recurring-defect procedure. Two more confirmed defects in the same protocol after the repairs in .8, .9, .10 and .13: (a) the server's framing record and Hyper's encoder asked the body separately, so a body whose size turned exact in between was framed by a length the record never saw; (b) admission settled a started body from whatever response it returned, although the handler can keep the body and return another. Classification: library design gap, not an implementation mistake. Both are further cases of two obligations the adapter reconstructs rather than owns: predicting Hyper's framing decision, and associating a body with the message that carries it. The local patches (shared head answers; a reach check on admission's size query) each close one case and leave residuals: off the registered server a body behind a layer that answers size_hint itself keeps its build-time framing; and item (1) above still holds, so a kept body dropped or queried inside another message's transport call adopts that message. Recommendation unchanged and stronger: assess reporting only body-observable facts. Still proposed and unexecuted; needs a user decision because it changes the documented completed/failed/dropped semantics.

Verification 2026-11-18 on the working tree over c211f01f (uncommitted), Rust 1.100.0: bash scripts/verify.sh exit 0 (fmt, file budget 0 errors, all four Clippy configurations, all six test-matrix parts, rustdoc, all HTTP smoke profiles). A first run failed Clippy on two lints in the new code (clone_on_copy, fn_params_excessive_bools); both fixed before the passing run. After that run only docs/status.md and the root AGENTS.md code map changed; file budget and the scripts matrix part were re-run and pass. Public-API surface (surface.py, rustdoc JSON, rustc 1.102.0-nightly 8eb778d04, separate target dirs): batter-axum 618 -> 625 entries, 0 removed, 7 added, all low_level::ForcedCloseIo. Limits: HTTP/2 not exercised; of upgraded connections only the I/O type and socket recovery are exercised; start_tests.rs now exceeds the 500-line warning threshold (514, under the 800 maximum). Not committed: awaiting an explicit request.

Decision 2026-11-18: the user delegated the choice ('best long-term decision for batter itself') after the ADR-010 report. Chosen and implemented in the working tree: an owned body's outcome follows only the length the response its builder returned declares, read once at the hand-over (Content-Length as plain digits with equal values, else the body's exact size; none for HEAD, 2xx CONNECT, 1xx, 204, 304), and what its source then does. Removed: the Hyper encoder/refusal mirror, Written and its thread-local, admission settlement and its reach check, the nested flag, HeadAnswers and the registered server's framing record (ConnectionBody again only holds the completion token). Rejected: pinning Hyper (leaves the association defects) and keeping only admission settlement (keeps the mechanism the last defect came from). Accepted costs: a refused head leaves the body dropped (INFO) where it was failed (WARN); a length added after the hand-over is not read. Residual recorded under ADR-010: declaring the length outside the builder still compiles and changes only the label. Record: ADR-008 amendment 2026-11-18; tests/streaming/sockets/undeclared.rs (3) and endings.rs (+1) assert the new contract; sockets/framing.rs, the head socket test, two destruction.rs cases and the mirror unit tests were deleted because they asserted the removed contract; start_tests.rs now tests the declared-length rule (3). This supersedes fixes (4) and (5) of batter-9wig.14, whose code is gone; fixes (1), (2), (3) and (6) stand. Verification pending.

Verification 2026-11-18 on the working tree over c211f01f (uncommitted), Rust 1.100.0: bash scripts/verify.sh exit 0 after the redesign (fmt, file budget 0 errors, four Clippy configurations, six test-matrix parts, rustdoc, HTTP smokes). Afterwards two test comments were corrected; fmt, file budget and the batter-axum streaming target (55 passed) were re-run. Public-API surface vs c211f01f: batter-axum 618 -> 625, 0 removed, 7 added (low_level::ForcedCloseIo only); the redesign changes no public item. Net diff vs HEAD: 24 files, +724/-2231. Limits: hand mutation checks from 2026-11-11..16 were not re-run against the new rule; HTTP/2 not exercised. Fallback: stash 'batter-9wig.14: six review fixes' holds the pre-redesign state. Not committed: awaiting an explicit request.

Superseded in part on 2026-11-18 by the batter-9wig.11 redesign in the same working tree: fixes (4) shared head answers and (5) carried-body settle were removed with the machinery they patched; (1), (2), (3) and (6) stand. Final verification is recorded on batter-9wig.11.

Follow-up review 2026-11-18, ForcedCloseIo (2 findings, both confirmed and fixed): the recovery example and the CHANGELOG before/after now return the downcast's read_buf beside the socket and consume it first, and tests/operational/forced_close/upgraded.rs sends six protocol bytes with the upgrade request and asserts they arrive in that buffer, through both registrations (6 repeated runs passed); get_ref and the type's obligations now state that I/O on the listener's own type, including through a shared reference, bypasses the forced close. The get_ref bypass is read from source, not exercised.

Follow-up review 2026-11-18 (2 findings, both confirmed and fixed in docs with tests): (a) the contract promised the same outcome in-process and on a server; only the rule is the same, since the outcome also depends on whether the holder stops polling (Hyper after a written length: dropped) or polls on (a collecting in-process holder: idle_timeout). New in-process test endings::a_collecting_holder_meets_an_outcome_a_transport_that_stops_does_not. (b) a refused head is not detected and is not always dropped: a pending body is dropped, an already ended one is completed. sockets::undeclared::a_head_the_transport_refuses_is_not_detected now covers both under a final 103. Review follow-up 2 (2026-11-18), two findings confirmed and fixed, uncommitted. (1) tests/operational/forced_close/upgraded.rs no longer asserts that Hyper buffered all six early bytes on a socket: TCP may split them. The socket test (both registrations) now asserts the peer, the payload echoed whole and in order, and only that the buffer is a prefix of it. New test bytes_read_with_the_upgrade_request_come_back_in_the_downcasts_buffer uses an in-memory one-connection listener (tokio duplex, register_http only): head plus three bytes in one write come back in read_buf exactly, the remaining three are written after the downcast is reported and read from the I/O. Upgrade tests run 30 times, all ok. (2) into_streaming_response rustdoc, README and docs/guarantees.md now say the request completion event's method and status tell only some dropped causes apart, not a transport stopping at a length added after hand-over from a peer disconnecting after the same bytes. Codex review loop (gpt-6.2-astra, xhigh; jig review-fix run 019951fa, commit mode none), 2026-11-18. Round 1: 11 findings, 6 causes, all confirmed and repaired. Round 2: 13 findings, 7 causes, all confirmed. RECURRING-DEFECT ASSESSMENT (ADR-010), recorded in ADR-008's amendment: (a) keeping the request's dispatcher in the shared ObservationState, added for the late-start refusal finding, produced a confirmed defect in three consecutive rounds (reached a later request with copied extensions; observer liveness did not prove provenance; kept the subscriber alive for as long as any copy of the extensions). Library design gap, not implementation mistakes: copyable request metadata was asked to prove which request an event belongs to. Decision: ObservationState holds no dispatcher; the body event's dispatcher is the one the request span itself names, else the one recorded on the private Admission at admission. Residual, documented and not exercised: a body started while a copied record's observer is still alive enters that observer's span (outside the supported redispatch). (b) three rounds each found an outcome example that omitted an input; the rustdoc, README and guarantees now state the complete rule once and give examples only as exercised HTTP/1 cases naming every input. Other round-2 repairs: HTTP/1 scope on downcast recovery; into_inner registry-removal unit test and in-flight-wake wording; deterministic wire test for a late ten-byte length; refused-head cases stated with prior polls. New tests: tests/streaming/subscribers.rs (4), forced_close unit test, undeclared.rs split and extended. Verification on the round-1 tree: verify.sh failed once in three Docker-backed runledger-test-support tests under host load (load average 36-49, 28 unrelated containers), passed on the controller's retry. Round-2 tree: fmt, file budget, clippy -p batter-axum and cargo test -p batter-axum pass; full verify pending in the controller.

Codex loop, rounds 3-4 (2026-11-18): round 3, 10 findings (8 causes); round 4, 11 findings (8 causes); all confirmed and repaired; verify.sh passed in the controller on the round-2 and round-3 trees (00014-validate, 00019-validate). Fourth recurrence in the subscriber family: the round-2 repair kept a strong Dispatch on the Admission record, itself a copyable extension. Final shape: ObservationState holds only the span while its observer lives; Admission holds a WeakDispatch; the event dispatcher is the published span's owner, else the upgraded weak admission dispatcher, else the one current at the hand-over; an ended body releases both dispatchers, also when its source's destructor unwinds. Other code fix: both bounds are checked after an empty frame's destruction before the end query. A fresh-context audit of every changed statement against source, tests and dependency sources found 17 more over-broad or stale statements, all applied. Process note: the first controller run (019951fa) ended SCOPE_CHANGED because repairs made during triage used up its three source reconciliations; a successor run on the stabilized checkout follows, with edits only inside repair assignments.

Codex loop continued (2026-11-18). Successor controller run 1daafa7c: round 5, 12 findings, all confirmed and repaired inside its repair step; verify.sh passed there on the repaired tree (00006-validate, fingerprint 91f35a1f); its follow-up review found 4 more (1 medium). That run then ended BLOCKED in its stall-recovery bookkeeping (my recovery diagnosis listed already-fixed findings), so the loop continues with 'codex review --uncommitted' run directly with the same model and effort. Code changes in round 5 and its follow-up: the hand-over asks the body's size only where the status and headers leave the declaration to it; a call of the application's body that unwound is terminal at poll, end and size entry points; the request observer unpublishes its span before calling the subscriber; the body's ending owns the source in an unwind-safe guard before emitting its event. Docs: bounds are stated as ending the body with an error at a poll, and what the peer sees only as exercised HTTP/1.1 cases. New tests in tests/streaming/unwinding.rs and subscribers.rs. Full verify.sh on the final tree is still owed.

Codex loop, direct 'codex review --uncommitted' rounds 6-15 (2026-11-18): findings per round 4, 4, 2, 2, 1, 1, 4, 2, 3, 3; all confirmed and repaired; uncommitted. They concern unwinding foreign code around the owned body's ending. Resulting shape: (1) streaming/end.rs holds one staged ending guard (source, kept answer, wait, task waker): armed before any call out, scope cancelled, span entered for the event, source destroyed inside the span, wait and task waker released, span left, request dispatcher dropped, kept answer released, hand-over dispatcher dropped; whichever stage unwinds, what is left is destroyed under the hand-over dispatcher. (2) Any unwind out of poll_frame or a query is the body's end: remembered, scope cancelled at once, next poll returns 'panicked' without entering the source. This changed one committed assertion (destruction.rs: the scope stayed live after a caught poll panic). (3) The body keeps the polling task's waker and polls its source, timer and cancellation wait only with a waker of its own, muted on unwinds and detached into the ending guard, so ending wakes nobody. (4) Hand-over asks the size lazily and drops the admission record before assembling the response; ForcedCloseIo::into_inner drops its registry entry before returning the I/O. (5) Files split for the 800-line budget: streaming/scope.rs, streaming/poll.rs, tests/streaming/unwinding/{kept,wakers}.rs; tests/body_teardown.rs is a separate binary for subscribers whose destructor panics.
